Run a model over many parameter sets

Source: R/run.R
run_parameter_sets.Rd

Simulate an odin2 model from its initial conditions, once for each of a collection of parameter sets such as posterior draws or scenarios. The result has the same structure as the output of monty::monty_sample(), so it can be passed to tidy_trajectories(), tidy_pars() and to monty's own tools such as monty::monty_samples_thin(). Use continue_parameter_sets() to carry on from the end of a fit or of a previous run.

Usage

run_parameter_sets(
  generator,
  pars,
  times,
  packer = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  n_particles = 1,
  deterministic = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  time_start = NULL,
  save_trajectories = TRUE,
  dt = NULL,
  ode_control = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  n_threads = 1
)

Arguments

generator

An odin2 model generator, as returned by odin2::odin(). When rerunning a fitted model, pass the filter or unfilter used for the fit instead: the model, its time step and start time, and whether it is deterministic are then taken from the fit rather than given again.

pars

The parameter sets. One of:

  • a monty_samples object (requires packer); chains are kept

  • a data frame with one row per parameter set and one numeric column per parameter. Columns .chain, .iteration and .draw, as produced by posterior::as_draws_df(), are not treated as parameters, and .chain is used to keep chains

  • a list of parameter lists; without a packer, elements that are the same in every set are treated as fixed

  • a matrix with one column per parameter set (requires packer)

times

Times to save output at, increasing and no earlier than time_start.

packer

A monty::monty_packer() used to convert between parameter vectors and the list of parameters the model needs. Required if pars is a monty_samples object or a matrix.

fixed

Optional named list of parameters held constant across all parameter sets, for example list(N = 1000). These are added to every set, and replace any fixed values in packer. They may not name a parameter that varies in pars.

n_particles

Number of particles (stochastic realisations) to run for each parameter set.

deterministic

Logical, indicating that a stochastic model should be run deterministically, replacing random draws with their expectations. Has no effect on ODE models, which are always deterministic. By default FALSE, or as the fit if generator is a filter or unfilter.

n_draws

Optional number of parameter sets to select at random from pars. If given, the result has a single chain.

time_start

The time at which the model starts. By default 0, or as the fit if generator is a filter or unfilter.

save_trajectories

Either TRUE, to save all state variables, or a character vector of variable names to save.

dt, ode_control

Time step for discrete-time models and control for ODE models, passed to dust2::dust_system_create(). By default those of the fit if generator is a filter or unfilter, and otherwise the model's defaults.

seed, n_threads

Passed to dust2::dust_system_create().

Value

An object of class monty_samples, with elements:

  • pars: parameters x samples x chains

  • density: samples x chains, all NA as no density is computed

  • observations$trajectories: state x time x samples x chains, or state x particle x time x samples x chains if n_particles > 1

  • observations$state: the final state, laid out as trajectories without the time dimension

Everything needed to tidy the result or continue the run is stored as an attribute, so tidy_trajectories() and continue_parameter_sets() need no further information.

Details

dust2 provides dust2::dust_system_simulate(), which runs a system that has already been created. This function does the work around that: turning the parameter sets into the form the model needs, creating a system with one group per parameter set, running it, and arranging the output so that each trajectory stays with the parameters that produced it.

All parameter sets are run together in a single dust2 system, so every set must produce a model with the same state (for example, the same array sizes).

To compare scenarios, call this once per scenario and combine the tidied results with dplyr::bind_rows(..., .id = "scenario"). For a counterfactual based on a fit, convert the samples to a data frame with posterior::as_draws_df(), change the parameters there, and pass the data frame as pars.
